speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and when did you first notice it?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash cause any itching or discomfort for the baby, and have you noticed any scaling or redness in the diaper area or skin folds? I would also like to examine the scalp closely to see if the scales are adherent or greasy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the greasy yellow scales and the infant's age, this presentation is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, also known as cradle cap. DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic dermatitis
